title: Provision CloudFront Distribution
scenario: Your platform team needs CloudFront Distribution for a global CDN in front of an origin. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_cloudfront_distribution.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_cloudfront_distribution resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_cloudfront_distribution.

hints.why: A CDN changes latency, caching and the public attack surface. Origin and cache settings are part of the application contract.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_cloudfront_distribution. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use CloudFront when content is served globally or when you need TLS, caching and origin protection in front of HTTP services.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "this"`. Use this code shape: enabled; tags; default_cache_behavior { viewer_protocol_policy }; viewer_certificate { minimum_protocol_version }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.project_name`, `var.environment`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
